title: Kumbhakarna wakes
hook: the giant who sleeps, and the three qualities in every heart
carry: tamas: seeing what's right, and sleeping through it

segments.voice: Yesterday: Lakshmana falls, Hanuman flies the mountain back, and Rama holds him like a brother. Bhakti.
screen: `BHAKTI: GOD HOLDS HIS DEVOTEE LIKE FAMILY.`

segments.voice: Everybody knows someone who's impossible to wake up. Ravana is losing. His generals are dead, his city is surrounded, and he has one option left. Deep in the palace, his brother is asleep: Kumbhakarna, a giant so huge that when he stands up, the story says, he's like a mountain walking. He sleeps for months at a time. So Ravana sends servants to wake him. A new week starts with the hardest alarm clock in literature.
screen: `IMPOSSIBLE TO WAKE.` → `THE GIANT ASLEEP IN THE PALACE.` → `THE HARDEST ALARM CLOCK.`

segments.voice: In Valmiki, waking him is almost comic. Demons pile mountains of food and jars of drink by his nose. They beat drums, blow conches, roar. They drive elephants over his body. Finally he yawns, and wakes up hungry. Why does he sleep like that? In Valmiki's last book, Ravana, Kumbhakarna and their younger brother Vibhishana each do fierce austerities, and the creator god Brahma offers each a boon. Ravana asks that no god or demon can kill him; he doesn't bother to mention humans. Kumbhakarna is about to ask, and the gods panic, so the goddess of speech, Sarasvati, enters his mouth, and out comes a wish for sleep. Later tellings make it a slip of one syllable: indrasana, Indra's throne, came out as nidrasana, a bed of sleep. And Vibhishana asks for this: that his mind stay on dharma, on what's right, even in the worst trouble. Three brothers, three wishes. Hindu teaching names three qualities, the gunas, woven through every person: sattva, clear and bright; rajas, restless wanting; tamas, heavy and dull, the pull to sleep. Many teachers read the brothers as those three: Ravana's rajas, Vibhishana's sattva, Kumbhakarna's tamas. Awake, the giant hears what Ravana has done and tells him straight: you were wrong to take Sita. This is your own doing. And then, out of loyalty to his brother, he goes out and fights for the wrong cause anyway, until Rama's arrows bring him down and his fall shakes the earth. That's tamas. Not stupidity: heaviness, darkness, the dulling of what you already know. All three live in each of us. Tamas is the part that knows you should call your grandmother back, and rolls over anyway.
screen: `DRUMS, ELEPHANTS, MOUNTAINS OF FOOD.` · `THREE BROTHERS, THREE WISHES.` · `SATTVA, RAJAS, TAMAS.` · `HE SEES IT. HE FIGHTS FOR IT ANYWAY.`

segments.voice: Hindu tradition prizes the hour before dawn, brahma muhurta, as the clearest time of day, the time of sattva. Sit up straight for two minutes and notice which of the three is loudest in you right now: clear, restless or heavy. Don't fight it; just name it. If you pray, ask for what Vibhishana asked for: a mind that stays on what's right, even in trouble. If you don't, picture tomorrow's alarm, and getting up the first time.
Kumbhakarna wakes. Ravana's giant brother, who tells him the truth and then fights for him anyway.
Your line: tamas, seeing what's right, and sleeping through it. Kumbhakarna saw. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Kumbhakarna's waking is a favorite, often comic scene in Ramlila plays and children's retellings, and in everyday Indian speech a heavy sleeper is sometimes teasingly called a Kumbhakarna.

original.note: Sanskrit: kumbha (pot) + karna (ear). The giant with ears like great pots.

Kumbhakarna.meaning: Ravana's giant brother, who slept for months at a time

Brahma.meaning: the creator god, who offered him a boon

Sarasvati.meaning: the goddess of speech, who entered his mouth

indrasana.meaning: Indra's throne, what he meant to ask for

nidrasana.meaning: a bed of sleep, what he asked for instead

Vibhishana.meaning: Ravana's younger brother, who asked for a mind fixed on dharma

gunas.meaning: the three qualities woven through every person

tamas.meaning: heaviness, dullness, the pull to sleep
